# kedi Programming Language

> A typed orchestration language for LLM programs.

Typed reference documentation for the Kedi language and Python API.
- [Home](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/index.md): A language for typed programs with natural language. Learn the syntax, follow the runtime, and find the rules behind your programs.

## Learn Kedi

- [Learn Kedi](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/getting-started/index.md): Start with Installation, then work through Your First Program. You will distinguish values computed by Python from values requested from a model, preserve their types across procedure calls, and use the result in ordinary control flow. Agents and tools come later, when the task needs them.
- [Installation](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/getting-started/installation.md): The core package requires Python 3.10 or newer and advertises Python 3.10 through 3.14. Optional integrations can require a newer interpreter; this is not a promise that every extra runs on every core-supported Python version.
- [First Program](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/getting-started/first-program.md): Your first program asks a model to complete a sentence, captures its answers as typed values, and uses those values in its output. No Python block or SDK call is needed.
- [Projects and Execution](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/getting-started/projects-and-execution.md): A .kedi file can contain top-level values, types, procedures, profiles, tests, evals, and the final executable statements. Single-file programs are a good fit when the public surface is small and all prompts share one lifecycle.
- [Find a Reference](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/index.md): This section is the compact, searchable inventory of Kedi's public language, runtime, Python, adapter, and tooling contracts. The conceptual sections linked from each table provide examples and rationale.

## Language Reference

- [Language Reference](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/index.md): A Kedi program is an ordered sequence of declarations and executable statements. The public language surface includes:

## Language Reference / Source and Syntax

- [Source Structure](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/source-structure.md): Kedi preserves source order for declarations and executable statements. Imports publish their exported bindings at the position of the import, and later writes replace earlier bindings:
- [Multiline Syntax and Escaping](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/multiline-and-escaping.md): Kedi has separate multiline rules for model prompts, rendered returns, Python, comments, and directives. Do not transfer one construct's continuation syntax to another.
- [Syntax Index](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/syntax.md): Declarations and executable statements retain source order. Indentation defines scope; tabs compare as width four, but spaces are recommended.
- [Directive Index](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/directives.md): Framework and harness selection are mutually exclusive in one state. Literal names are statically validated; backtick expressions defer validation to runtime. Adapter settings unsupported by the selected backend are filtered or rejected according to that adapter's contract.

## Language Reference / Values and Types

- [Types and Constraints](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/types.md): Kedi types are runtime contracts, provider schemas, and editor information. They are used in output fields, variable initializations, procedure signatures, custom fields, tool schemas, evals, and the Python API. Assignments reuse the target binding's established type contract.
- [Outputs and Bindings](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/outputs-and-assignments.md): Square brackets are write syntax in Kedi. In a >> template they declare fields the model must produce; on the left of = they initialize variables with deterministic values. Neither form is the same as <name>, which reads a value.
- [Scopes and Binding Lifetime](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/scopes-and-bindings.md): A binding belongs to the scope that declares it. A procedure invocation, a selected branch, and each loop iteration have their own value environments. Visibility is not ownership: seeing an outer value does not make a new local declaration overwrite it.

## Language Reference / Model Interaction

- [Templates and Invokes](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/templates-and-invokes.md): >> opens a model template at top level or inside a procedure:
- [Substitutions and Calls](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/substitutions-and-calls.md): Substitutions are Kedi's read syntax. They insert an existing value, a procedure result, or a Python expression into rendered text. They never declare an output.

## Language Reference / Procedures

- [Procedures and Closures](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/procedures.md): Procedures package Kedi statements into typed, reusable callables. They are also the unit exposed to tools, tests, evals, optimization, generated code, and the Python API.
- [Parameters and Returns](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/parameters-and-returns.md): Procedure signatures define the native contract between Kedi, Python, tools, tests, and evals. An omitted annotation is not Any: it defaults to str.

## Language Reference / Control Flow

- [Branches and Claims](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/control-flow.md): Kedi supports deterministic and model-classified branches, conditional loops, and sequential iterable loops. A trailing : after an inline Python condition selects deterministic execution. Without that trailing colon, the header is a Kedi template claim classified by the active agent adapter.
- [Loops and Map](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/core-language/loops-and-map.md): Conditional loops repeat a condition; iterable loops visit values; map adds a continuation per retained iteration. None creates an implicit result collection.

## Language Reference / Python Interop

- [Python Interop](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-interop/index.md): Python is Kedi's deterministic execution layer. Use it for arithmetic, validation, data shaping, library calls, control flow, and local side effects; use Kedi templates where model judgement is required.
- [Inline Expressions](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-interop/inline-expressions.md): Inline Python is a single expression enclosed in one pair of backticks. It is evaluated in the active Kedi runtime environment.
- [Python Blocks](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-interop/python-blocks.md): Fenced Python blocks execute statement suites. They are the right boundary for control flow, local imports, multiple calculations, exception handling, and deterministic integration code.
- [Prelude and Scope](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-interop/prelude-globals-and-scope.md): The prelude establishes shared Python state before Kedi declarations and statements are compiled. Ordinary blocks, by contrast, are isolated execution units whose new Python locals do not persist.

## Language Reference

- [Coverage and Limitations](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/semantic-coverage.md): This map summarizes the language and runtime surfaces covered by the manual. It is not a claim that every adapter implements every capability. Use the capability matrix for backend support and Find a Reference to reach the contract for a particular operation.

## Modules and Packages

- [Modules and Packages](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/modules-and-packaging/index.md): Kedi modules split a program into explicit public surfaces. Packages distribute one module tree through the local Kedi registry; they do not change the module language.

## Modules and Packages / Module System

- [Modules and Resolution](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/modules-and-packaging/modules.md): A module is a .kedi source file compiled as part of a root program. Its top-level code initializes module state; its export directive selects which bindings are published to importers.
- [Imports and Exports](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/modules-and-packaging/imports-and-exports.md): Imports publish selected module bindings directly into the current source environment. Exports are explicit so implementation helpers remain private.

## Modules and Packages / Standard Modules

- [Built-In Modules](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/modules-and-packaging/built-in-modules.md): Kedi ships a small set of ordinary .kedi modules. They use the same explicit exports, profiles, Python interop, tool metadata, and resolution rules as project modules.
- [Filesystem](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/modules-and-packaging/filesystem.md): Import the tools you need or apply a profile. Workspace containment, secret-file opt-in, risk classification, and approval are separate checks; ordinary Python execution is not sandboxed by this module.
- [Example Modules](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/modules-and-packaging/example-modules.md): These modules demonstrate Kedi composition. Importing them can execute Python setup; they are not guaranteed to work in a headless or dependency-free host.

## Modules and Packages / Distribution

- [Package Manifests](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/modules-and-packaging/package-manifests.md): package.kedi is a declarative package manifest written in Kedi directive syntax. It is not an executable module.
- [Build a Local Package](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/modules-and-packaging/local-package.md): This deterministic package has no model or third-party Python dependency. It separates a public module entry point from an implementation module.
- [Installation and Registries](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/modules-and-packaging/installation-and-registries.md): Kedi installs package source into a user-local registry. Installation validates the manifest, Python compatibility, source containment, file kinds, and bounded tree size before replacing an existing installed copy.
- [Manifest Reference](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/package-manifest.md): The file must be named exactly package.kedi, contain exactly one package directive, and contain no imports, exports, procedures, types, Python, values, or executable statements. Comments are allowed.

## Agents and Orchestration

- [Agents and Orchestration](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/index.md): Kedi treats model execution as scoped agent configuration rather than a global string. A scope can select a framework or harness, model, reasoning effort, instructions, settings, tools, MCP servers, skills, approvals, and child agents.

## Agents and Orchestration / Profiles and Configuration

- [Instructions and Settings](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/instructions-and-settings.md): Instructions define agent behavior; settings define adapter/model mechanics. Both are lexical and apply to following calls.
- [Profiles and Composition](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/profiles.md): Profiles can also select a lexical native history processor through > history: with enabled: true and processor: callback . This overrides the adapter constructor default only for the scoped invocation. See History Processing for callback types, explicit disable, safe group retention, and lineage.
- [Agent Scope and Capabilities](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/scoping-and-capabilities.md): Agent state follows lexical source scope. Capability metadata determines whether the selected adapter can honor the resulting contract.

## Agents and Orchestration / Tools and Permissions

- [Procedure and Python Tools](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/tools-and-use.md): > use: exposes a callable as an agent tool or applies a profile. Its block form registers tools only.
- [MCP Tools](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/mcp.md): > mcp: attaches one Model Context Protocol server to the active agent state. The selected adapter translates the normalized specification into its MCP client/toolset surface.
- [Skills](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/skills.md): Skills are scoped instruction documents loaded on demand through two read-only tools. Kedi does not inject every skill into every prompt.
- [Approval Policies](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/approvals.md): Approvals mediate individual tool calls after arguments are produced and before the tool executes. They are not model-output validation and do not sandbox ordinary embedded Python.
- [Tool Reasons and LLM Approval](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/tool-reasons.md): A tool justification is model-provided context for the approval handler. It is not authorization, a new tool effect, or a separate reasoning-model call. The feature is disabled by default and applies only to tools that may require approval.

## Agents and Orchestration / Lifecycle

- [Lifecycle Hooks](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/hooks.md): Hooks let application code observe or govern agent boundaries without moving that policy into model instructions. They are synchronous with the boundary: the run waits for each handler before it continues.
- [Stream Events](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/stream-events.md): Kedi exposes completed semantic agent messages as an adapter-neutral event stream. This lets a terminal, editor, web UI, or orchestrator show useful progress while the authoritative adapter call continues normally.

## Agents and Orchestration / Subagents and Workflows

- [Subagents](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/subagents.md): Subagents let a profile delegate bounded, isolated work to explicitly declared children. The parent chooses a task; the child runs with its own configuration and returns evidence or a typed result. It is not an implicit ability to spawn any profile or inspect the parent's local variables.
- [Native Tasks and Await](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/subagent-tasks.md): Use > task when the program decides which child to call. Unlike model-driven delegate_task, this does not require a parent model request to choose a tool. The selected parent profile must explicitly declare that direct child.
- [Typed Child Results](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/subagent-results.md): A parent receives a result envelope, not the child's local environment. Decide whether the child should return prose or a validated value before choosing the delegation interface.
- [Foreground and Background Runs](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/subagent-lifecycle.md): Delegation tools are model-facing tools added to the parent's profile. Native > task / > await statements and runtime.subagents(...) are separate program-controlled entry points to the same coordinator. The tool names below describe the schema that the model sees.
- [Concurrent Result Processing](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/subagent-processing.md): Start child tasks with > task, then handle their results as they finish. Unlike sequential > await statements, a task group does not make a ready result wait behind an earlier, slower child.
- [Limits, Isolation and Safety](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/subagent-limits.md): Delegation has several independent bounds. Increasing one does not increase the others, and a profile cannot remove a runtime safety ceiling.
- [Continuations and Persistence](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/subagent-continuations.md): Use a continuation when a completed child should refine earlier work. Use a new delegation when the task should start without that conversation.
- [Dynamic Workflows](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/dynamic-workflows.md): Delegate mode lets the parent choose one child call at a time. Dynamic mode lets it write a bounded orchestration program over its declared children. This is useful for dependency graphs, concurrent independent work, and typed result composition; it does not grant access to arbitrary profiles.
- [Python Embedding](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/subagent-python.md): The language declares the profile graph. Python supplies the adapter, host tools, global values, resource limits, and runtime lifetime. It does not need to reach into the coordinator or call an invented kedi.subagent() function.
- [Reviewed Evidence Workflow](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/reviewed-evidence.md): This example connects the whole boundary: a parent delegates, a child reads a local fixture, the child returns a typed result, and the parent writes a report through an approval handler. The parent cannot read the fixture directly; the child cannot write the report.

## Agents and Orchestration / CodeMode

- [CodeMode](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/codemode.md): CodeMode lets a model discover tools and process intermediate results without putting each intermediate result in its conversation. Instead of sending every application tool schema to the model, Kedi exposes three stable control tools and keeps selected tool execution inside a bounded Monty sandbox.
- [Sandbox Limits and Recovery](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/codemode-sandbox.md): CodeMode is bounded execution over hydrated tools, not general host Python. The model must discover a tool and request its schema before using it unless the application explicitly lists that exact exposed name in preload_tools. See Discovery and Execution for that protocol.

## Context and Runtime

- [Context and Runtime](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/index.md): The runtime turns Kedi source into a validated program, compiles declarations and scopes, executes deterministic statements, and crosses the model boundary only at explicit template or raw-invoke statements.

## Context and Runtime / Execution

- [Execution and Dataflow](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/execution-and-dataflow.md): Kedi executes source in order while preserving lexical declaration state. Concurrency changes scheduling, not the declared value and type contracts. It does not promise identical stochastic outputs or side-effect ordering.
- [Concurrency](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/concurrency.md): Kedi runs independent model templates concurrently by default on a bounded, shared pool of eight workers. Dependent calls wait for the values they need. No environment variable or special syntax is required.
- [Run Budgets](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/run-budgets.md): A run budget bounds managed work across one root invocation, its procedures, and its subagents. It is an execution ceiling, not an estimate of token usage or a provider billing limit.
- [Incremental Execution](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/interactive-execution.md): Interactive execution evaluates complete Kedi fragments against one persistent, process-local runtime. It is useful for terminal exploration, notebooks, debuggers, and hosts that need to submit code incrementally without replaying earlier cells.

## Context and Runtime / Context Management

- [Artifacts](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/tool-artifacts.md): Tool Artifacts is Kedi's bounded large-value transport. It prevents large tool results and generated fields from being copied into model context while preserving the original typed value for Kedi and embedded Python.
- [Admission and Configuration](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/artifact-policy.md): Choose which values enter storage and how much context each preview or read may expose. These are byte and character limits, not provider token budgets.
- [Reading and Querying](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/artifact-retrieval.md): A reference means the producer already ran. Inspect that stored result instead of repeating the source tool.
- [Reducing Artifact Data](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/artifact-reduction.md): This model-assisted example combines two tool results. It requires a tool-capable model; a requested strategy does not guarantee the model follows it.
- [Storage and Lifetime](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/artifact-lifecycle.md): Context reduction, producer memory, persistent storage, and history are separate concerns. Close the owning session when finished.
- [Artifact Safety](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/artifact-safety.md): Bounded references do not make source tools, embedded Python, or sensitive payloads safe to execute or disclose.
- [Conversation History](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/history.md): History retains successful turns. It is not response memoization: a new prompt still invokes the model.
- [Compaction](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/compaction.md): Custom retention and transformation use the separate processor history field, not a new compaction_mode. If exact archival and processing are both configured, archival runs first and its checkpoint remains protected from the processor.
- [Provider Prefix Caching](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/prefix-cache.md): Provider prompt caching reuses computation for a matching request prefix. It does not skip a model invocation and is independent of Kedi's response cache.
- [Application Caches](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/caching.md): Kedi has several independent reuse mechanisms. Enabling one does not enable the others.

## Context and Runtime / Observability

- [Telemetry](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/telemetry.md): Kedi provides a dependency-free telemetry seam in the runtime. It is a no-op until the separate opentelemetry-instrumentation-kedi package installs an OpenTelemetry backend. Application code keeps ownership of the OpenTelemetry SDK, resource, sampler, exporter, and shutdown lifecycle.
- [Errors and Tracebacks](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/runtime/errors-and-debugging.md): Kedi reports failures in the language that owns the failing operation. Parse diagnostics point to Kedi syntax, runtime failures carry Kedi execution frames, and embedded Python tracebacks are mapped back from generated Python to the original .kedi source.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/diagnostics-and-troubleshooting.md): Kedi distinguishes parse, compile, capability, execution, validation, and external-backend failures. Preserve the rendered source location and original exception when reporting a problem.

## Python API

- [Python API](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/index.md): The Python API embeds Kedi programs in typed Python callables. It preserves the same template, substitution, output, profile, tool, MCP, approval, skills, artifact, conversation, and runtime semantics as .kedi files.

## Python API / Calling Kedi

- [Query Decorator](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/query.md): A query function's docstring must start with a standalone kedi line:
- [Bind Decorator](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/bind.md): bind connects a Python signature to a complete .kedi program:

## Python API / Configuration

- [Configuration and Context](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/configuration-and-context.md): Native history processing can be scoped with AgentProfile(history_processing=HistoryProcessingSettings(processor=callback)), where both types are imported from kedi.agent_profile. An omitted policy inherits; HistoryProcessingSettings(processor=None) explicitly disables it. Pydantic and LangChain retain their history_processor= constructor defaults outside the override. See History. HistoryProcessingSettings(condition=predicate, inherit_processor=True) gates the inherited processor. Both adapters also accept history_processor_condition=predicate at construction; it requires an active processor and defaults to unconditional processing. Replacing a scoped processor without a condition clears the old condition.
- [Public Parameters](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/public-parameters.md): This reference distinguishes profile configuration from runtime construction. Names below are checked against the Python call signatures in the documentation test suite. Omitted selection values inherit; omission is not always equivalent to explicitly passing None.

## Python API / Integration

- [Types and Tools](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/types-and-tools.md): @kedi.type makes Python classes usable in Kedi output annotations and Python expressions:
- [Permissions and External Tools](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/approvals-mcp-and-skills.md): Decorate a handler to install it as the current Python API configuration's default dynamic policy:
- [MCP Configuration](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/mcp.md): Configure external tool servers through typed specifications. The following construction snippets require your installed server or running endpoint; they do not start a bundled Kedi service.
- [Skill Discovery](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/skills.md): Skills expose discoverable instruction files. They do not grant filesystem, tool, or approval permissions.
- [Hook Registration](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/hooks.md): Hooks intercept supported agent events. They differ from stream-event observers: selected hooks can edit or deny an operation.

## Python API / State and Execution

- [Artifacts and Sessions](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/artifacts-and-sessions.md): The Python API exposes the same artifact policy as > artifacts: and an explicit session boundary for calls that must share conversation history.
- [Decision Evidence](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/decisions.md): Decision evidence describes a completed evaluation without replacing its typed result. It is available only when the selected model integration supplies it; Kedi does not fabricate probability metadata for ordinary generated booleans.
- [Cache Control](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/cache-control.md): These helpers inspect process-local parse and response caches only. They do not control provider prompt caching.
- [Concurrency and Promises](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/concurrency-and-promises.md): Python API execution uses promise-pipelined concurrent template calls by default. Adjust the shared worker bound globally:
- [Runtime and Executors](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/caching-runtime-and-executors.md): See Inspect Cache State.
- [Embedding and Ownership](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/embedding.md): Use query for a procedure body, bind for a complete file, and interactive for incremental fragments. Low-level compilation is appropriate when the host owns source loading, execution, and resource cleanup.
- [Executor Protocol](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/executors.md): An executor owns embedded-Python execution. Replacing it must preserve environment, return, and error contracts; an interface stub is not a secure sandbox.

## Python API

- [API Reference](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/python-api.md): All stable high-level names below are imported from kedi.
- [Public Export Index](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/python-api/public-exports.md): History-specific exports live in kedi.agent_adapter: HistoryProcessorContext, HistoryProcessorState, HistoryProcessorCallback, HistoryProcessorCondition, HistoryOrigin, HistoryProcessingError, and HistoryProcessingValidationError. HistoryProcessingSettings is exported from kedi.agent_profile. See History.

## Models and Integrations

- [Models and Integrations](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/index.md): Adapters translate Kedi's uniform prompt contract into a model framework or an agent harness. Selection is explicit because those backends have materially different capabilities.

## Models and Integrations / Selection

- [Backend Selection](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/backend-selection.md): Kedi separates framework adapters from agent harnesses because they expose different execution and capability contracts.
- [Models and Reasoning](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agentic-engineering/models-and-reasoning.md): Model and reasoning directives refine the active backend. They do not select a framework or harness by themselves.
- [Codex Model Connections](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/codex-models.md): Codex Responses provides model access inside a framework adapter. This is different from Codex App Server, which runs an agent harness. Choosing a model route does not switch the surrounding agent framework.
- [Capability Matrix](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/capability-matrix.md): Capabilities are declared contracts, not feature guesses. Kedi validates the active profile against them and fails when a required surface is unavailable.

## Models and Integrations / Framework Adapters

- [Pydantic AI](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/pydantic-ai.md): Pydantic AI is a core Kedi dependency:
- [LangChain](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/langchain.md): Install the optional LangChain integrations:
- [DSPy](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/dspy.md): DSPy is an optional integration:

## Models and Integrations / Agent Harnesses

- [Codex App Server](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/codex.md): The Codex adapter starts:
- [Claude Agent SDK](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/claude.md): Install the optional SDK:
- [ACP Agents](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/acp.md): The generic ACP adapter launches an Agent Client Protocol process and speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio:
- [A2A Cloud Agents](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/a2a.md): Kedi can serve an exported agent profile as a remote A2A agent and can use any compatible A2A agent as an agent-harness. The coordinator may stay local while repository work, browser automation, or other expensive execution runs in a remote sandbox.
- [A2A Structured Output Protocol](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/a2a/extensions/structured-output/v1.md): https://docs.kedi-lang.org/a2a/extensions/structured-output/v1/

## Models and Integrations / Decision Models

- [TypeSafe Jev](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/typesafe.md): Jev evaluates claims, selects finite options, and scores described rubrics. It is not a free-form text generator. Kedi exposes it through the Pydantic AI and LangChain adapters using the optional kedi-typesafe package.
- [Claims and Thresholds](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/jev-claims.md): A claim asks for a decision, not generated prose. Its acceptance threshold is application policy, not a proof that the claim is true.
- [Criteria and Output Types](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/jev-criteria.md): Describe finite choices, binary evidence, probabilities, and ordered score levels. Import metadata through Python aliases; the Kedi type grammar does not gain arbitrary function calls.
- [Finite Extraction](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/jev-extraction.md): Extraction enumerates candidate text locally and asks Jev to select among those candidates. It is not unconstrained string generation and cannot produce a missing address or identifier by inference.
- [Decision Evidence](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/jev-evidence.md): Inspect the evaluation that produced a binding without changing the binding's native type or making another provider call. For a field-by-field API reference, see Decision Evidence.
- [Tool Selection](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/jev-tools.md): Tool selection is a finite decision. Argument generation and execution remain separate operations with their own validation and approval boundaries.
- [Generate, Evaluate, Route](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/jev-workflow.md): A generative model writes a draft; Jev evaluates it against explicit evidence; Kedi selects the next operation. Neither the draft nor a high probability is permission to send a message or perform a financial action.

## Models and Integrations / Extending Kedi

- [Custom Adapters](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/custom-adapters.md): Implement AgentAdapter[T] from kedi.agent_adapter:
- [Artifact Integration](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/agent-adapters/artifact-contract.md): An adapter must preserve the distinction between application values and model-visible artifact references. Ordinary Kedi/Python callers still receive native typed results; a model receives bounded metadata and retrieval tools.

## Testing and Optimization

- [Testing and Optimization](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/evals-and-optimization/index.md): Kedi separates four related jobs: deterministic tests, dataset-driven evaluation, prompt optimization, and AI-generated procedure implementations. They use some of the same procedures and Python environment, but they do not have the same purpose or lifecycle.

## Testing and Optimization / Validation

- [Test Blocks](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/evals-and-optimization/test-blocks.md): A test suite is a top-level block named after the procedure it validates. Each case has a unique label and contains Python code:
- [Evaluation Suites](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/evals-and-optimization/evaluation-suites.md): An evaluation suite belongs at top level and names the procedure being scored:
- [Datasets and Metrics](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/evals-and-optimization/datasets-and-metrics.md): A training dataset is Python code that returns an iterable:
- [Validation Workflow](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/evals-and-optimization/validation-workflow.md): This program needs no model or credentials. It distinguishes a regression test from a dataset score, with explicit expected values and failure feedback.

## Testing and Optimization / Optimization

- [Prompt Optimization](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/evals-and-optimization/prompt-optimization.md): An optimize span is an executable template block inside a procedure:
- [GEPA](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/evals-and-optimization/gepa.md): GEPA reflectively evolves prompt instructions from execution traces, metric scores, and feedback. Use it when:
- [Reproducible Comparisons](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/evals-and-optimization/reproducibility.md): An optimizer producing an artifact is not evidence that the program improved. Compare the complete executable procedure, not just the optimized text.

## Tools and Environments

- [Tools and Environments](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/index.md): Kedi ships one CLI, an LSP server, editor integrations, package commands, and low-level browser/playground bridges.

## Tools and Environments / Command Line

- [Run and Parse](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/run-and-parse.md): Kedi loads imports, optimized prompts, generates missing > auto: procedures, compiles, and runs the top-level program.
- [Test, Eval and Optimize](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/test-eval-and-optimize.md): Runs every @test: case and exits 1 if any fail.
- [Package Commands](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/package-commands.md): From a package root:
- [CLI Reference](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/cli.md): Use kedi --help, kedi install --help, or kedi add --help for the relevant usage surface.
- [Environment Variables](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/reference/environment-variables.md): KEDI_ADAPTER and KEDI_AGENT are mutually exclusive. Python configure(), decorator arguments, source directives, and CLI options can provide more local selection. KEDI_PARALLEL accepts 0/1, true/false, on/off, or a positive worker count; invalid values fail rather than silently selecting a mode. Unset or empty enables concurrency with eight workers. Use KEDI_PARALLEL=0 for sequential execution; no variable is needed to enable concurrency.

## Tools and Environments / Editors

- [Language Server](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/language-server.md): Equivalent fallback:
- [VS Code](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/vscode.md): Install **Kedi-Lang** (dyigitpolat.kedi-vscode) and the Microsoft Python extension. VS Code 1.85 or newer is required.
- [Zed](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/zed.md): Open **Zed → Extensions**, search for **Kedi**, and install it. For local development choose **Install Dev Extension** and select the kedi-zed directory, not the grammar repository.

## Tools and Environments / Interactive Environments

- [Terminal REPL](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/repl.md): The terminal submits complete fragments to an incremental runtime. For embedding, persistence restrictions, and failures, see Incremental Execution.
- [Local Notebook](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/notebook.md): Kedi Notebook is a local browser interface over InteractiveSession. It keeps definitions, values, imports, profiles, conversation state, and artifacts available across cells without concatenating or replaying earlier source.
- [Notebook Runtimes](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/notebook-runtimes.md): The Kedi compiler, interactive session and model adapters run in the local server. The runtime menu selects where embedded Python executes, not a place to move all Kedi execution or inference. Browser mode still needs that server.
- [Notebook Files and Recovery](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/notebook-files.md): The Save command offers two .kedinb modes:
- [Browser and Playground](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/browser-and-playground.md): Kedi parsing/compilation can remain on a Python backend while embedded Python and model inference are delegated through bridges. This avoids pretending the entire Python runtime or provider SDK runs natively in the browser.

## Cookbook

- [Cookbook](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/examples/index.md): These examples combine Kedi features into reviewable programs. Read the focused language pages first when you need a complete rule rather than a guided scenario.
- [Incident Triage Application](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/examples/complete-program.md): This compact application combines typed extraction, deterministic Python, procedure tools, profiles, command-line input, tests, and evals without hiding the boundaries between them.
- [Structured Extraction](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/examples/structured-extraction.md): This example extracts one reusable native object rather than parsing JSON text after a model call.
- [Tools and Approvals](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/examples/tools-and-approvals.md): This program exposes a read-only lookup and a mutating report writer. A dynamic approval handler redirects writes into a controlled directory.
- [Typed Agent Delegation](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/examples/agent-delegation.md): Subagents are explicit direct-child profiles. They are appropriate when a coordinator needs an isolated conversation, tool set, model, or safety policy; they are unnecessary for deterministic helper procedures.
- [Evaluation and Optimization](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/examples/evaluation-and-optimization.md): This example exposes one extraction prompt to supervised optimization with a metric that returns both a score and actionable feedback. Whether it improves requires measurement; the listing is not evidence of a quality gain.
- [Building a Kedi Package](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/examples/modules-and-packaging.md): This example creates a package whose public surface contains a type and two procedures while its parsing helper remains private.

## Benchmarks / Terminal-Bench 2.1

- [Reproduction Guide](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/terminal-bench.md): Kedi can run through Harbor's custom-agent interface for Terminal-Bench 2.1. The integration owns the Kedi harness, terminal tools, non-interactive approval policy, history, artifacts, and durable Kedi records. Harbor continues to own the dataset, task containers, resource limits, timeouts, graders, task lock, and job resume lifecycle.
- [Published Results](https://docs.kedi-lang.org/tooling/terminal-bench-results.md): This page reports two complete, single-trial Terminal-Bench 2.1 engineering runs. Every one of the 89 tasks was attempted once in each run. The runs use the same frozen Kedi harness, model, prompt, task set, resource split, timeout, and sandbox provider; the adapter is the subject difference.
